title: Townhall framing + FAQ scratch (CEO) - Mohit
summary: Scratch notes for CEO segment: framing a roadmap pivot toward Optimize first, prepping likely Qs and short honest answers. Includes talking bullets, triage Qs, and follow-ups.
content:
Topline framing (30s):
- We prioritized reliability, latency, and cost predictability since day one. Over the past 6 months we learned that customers value predictable unit economics more than headline throughput.
- Quick callout: were shifting the near-term roadmap to accelerate Redwood Optimize and routing/fallback polish so customers can safely reduce costs without quality regressions.
- Why: measurable unit-economics wins -> faster adoption + fewer escalations. Also buys time to finish the AI safety/regression work on the new sampler.

Key bullets for CEO (conversational):
- "We heard you. High-perf models are great but if the bill or latency surprises, people cant ship. So were focusing on levers that immediately improve predictability for customers."
- "This isn't cancelling our model investments; it's prioritizing shipable product that unlocks growth."
- "We will be transparent about the tradeoffs and share concrete numbers in the follow-up post."

Callouts / red lines (what to avoid saying):
- Dont commit to exact dates for major features in the townhall. We can commit to milestones: beta in X weeks, public rollout later.
- Avoid technical deep dives (leave that to product/eng AMA). Keep CEO messaging strategic.

Anticipated hard Qs + short answers (prep Q&A owner in parens):
1) "Does this mean other projects are cancelled?" (Product)
- Short: No cancellations; reprioritization. Were moving work forward that most directly reduces customer pain and unlocks revenue.

2) "Will this impact Dedicated or Private customers?" (Solutions Eng / Sales)
- Short: No negative impact on existing contracts. Dedicated/Private customers remain supported; were rolling optimizations in a way that respects SLAs and data controls.

3) "Are layoffs coming as part of this change?" (People Ops / CEO)
- Short: No. This is a roadmap priority shift. Were reallocating focus, not shrinking the team. If headcount changes become necessary we will be transparent and follow our people-first process.

4) "How will this affect latency/accuracy tradeoffs?" (Eng)
- Short: The goal is to preserve output quality while reducing cost/latency variance. Some experimental quantization/quantized runtime paths will be opt-in until validated with customer evals.

5) "What does success look like?" (Biz Ops)
- Short: measurable: 20-30% reduction in per-token cost for targeted workloads, 95th percentile latency improvement on interactive routes, and fewer customer escalations on bills.

Notes to self / TODOs before all-hands:
- Get a one-page with 2 charts: cost/unit before vs after (simulated) and customer escalation count trend (Rowan).
- Confirm exact phrasing on Dedicated guarantee (Legal review).
- Prep 2 slide speaker notes for Product lead showing A/B of old vs new routing policy (Aisha).
- Draft post-townhall FAQ doc (this will become canonical).

Slack/sequence plan (high-level):
- Townhall live -> CEO 10m -> Product 8m -> Quick AMA 20m -> Follow-up FAQ doc posted to #company-comms within 24h.
- Post the data appendix to confluence (link above).

Open questions (should resolve before townhall):
- Are we comfortable publishing simulated cost numbers, or do we need a controlled customer beta first? (Eng/Product)
- Legal: any contractual implications for customers on Dedicated? (Legal)
- Exec alignment: do all execs agree on the "not a layoff" script? (CEO + People Ops)

Tone guidance (short): honest, operator-focused, pragmatic, avoid marketing spin. Emphasize customer impact and operational discipline.

Rough script (CEO first 3mins):
- "Quick context: last year we doubled down on model performance. That was the right bet for capabilities. Over the last quarter weve seen a consistent pattern: teams ship faster and happier when their inference costs and latency are predictable. So were shifting short-term focus to product work that meaningfully reduces unit economics and removes friction for customers.
- "What this looks like: accelerating Redwood Optimize, improving routing & fallback behavior, and rolling out guarded quantization profiles for well-understood workloads.
- "What it doesnt mean: were not abandoning model research or our long-term investments. Were rebalancing.
- "Well publish a follow-up with specifics in 24 hours and open a customer beta next week."

Sticky phrasing options (pick one):
- "Prioritizing the levers that let our customers ship with confidence."
- "From headline perf to predictable economics."

Backchannel notes: keep product/eng executive on a single Slack thread for last-minute Qs. Ill consolidate and send final to CEO today EOD.

---
This is a scratchpad: incomplete, rough bullets, possible phrasing. Still need Legal check, Product numbers, and slides.

Notes to self: finalize FAQ skeleton, schedule dry-run with CEO + Product + People Ops tomorrow morning.
